questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Heart relation to thoracic cavity. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Positioned on the right side of the chest cavity
Positioned on the left side of the chest cavity
Positioned within the thoracic cavity beneath the sternum
questions.explanation: Of the options, this best captures the heart’s retrosternal, mediastinal location — it sits in the mediastinum directly behind (beneath) the body of the sternum. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How is the long axis in relation to the heart?
options: Creates cross-sectional segments of the ventricles
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through the left ventricle and atrium
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through both ventricles and atria from base to apex
Aligned with the line connecting the LV apex and the centre of the aortic valve
questions.explanation: The long-axis plane runs along the line joining the LV apex and the centre of the aortic valve, transecting the LV lengthwise. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How is the 4-Chamber in relation to the heart?
options: Creates cross-sectional segments of the ventricles
Aligned with the line connecting the LV apex and the centre of the aortic valve
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through the left ventricle and atrium
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through both ventricles and atria from base to apex
questions.explanation: The 4-chamber plane is perpendicular to the short axis and cuts through both ventricles and both atria from base to apex. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How is the 2-Chamber in relation to the heart?
options: Creates cross-sectional segments of the ventricles
Aligned with the line connecting the LV apex and the centre of the aortic valve
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through both ventricles and atria from base to apex
Perpendicular to the short-axis plane, slicing through the left ventricle and atrium
questions.explanation: The 2-chamber plane is perpendicular to the short axis but passes through only the left-sided chambers — the LV and LA. *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  How do you optimize your image by bringing the anatomy of interest centred in the field of view?
options: Slide your transducer from side to side
Rock  your transducer from side to side
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Rock  your transducer from side to side as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which of the following are tools to use when optimizing your image?
questions.explanation: Patient positioning, breathing maneuvers (e.g., held expiration), and contrast all improve image quality — so all three apply. *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the patient position for the parasternal window?
options: Left lateral decubitus with the left arm raised under the head
Right lateral decubitus with the right arm raised under the head
questions.explanation: Left lateral decubitus with the left arm raised brings the heart toward the chest wall, displaces lung, and widens the intercostal spaces. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What intercostal space is utilized for placement of the transducer in the parasternal window?
questions.explanation: The parasternal transducer is placed in the left 3rd–4th intercostal space, immediately adjacent to the sternum. *(Practice review slide 17.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which of the following is NOT a standard view seen in the parasternal window?
questions.explanation: The 5-chamber is an apical-window view, not a parasternal one, so it is the odd one out. *(Practice review slide 19.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What leaflet/s of the mitral valve are you seeing in the parasternal long-axis view?
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Anterior and posterior leaflet as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 21.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which of the following views does NOT show the pulmonic valve?
options: PSSAX at the level of the aortic valve
questions.explanation: The standard parasternal long-axis (of the LV) does not include the pulmonic valve — you see the LV, LA, aortic root, and mitral valve. *(Practice review slide 23.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Where should the indicator be pointing in the PSSAX window?
options: Toward the patient’s left shoulder (90 degrees clockwise from PLAX view)
questions.explanation: In the parasternal short-axis, the orientation marker points toward the patient’s left shoulder. *(Practice review slide 25.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using Figure 1, which cusp is the Non-coronary cusp?
questions.explanation: The non-coronary cusp (NCC) sits posteromedially, adjacent to the interatrial septum — cusp 3 in the figure. *(Practice review slide 27.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using Figure 1, which cusp is the Right coronary cusp?
questions.explanation: The right coronary cusp (RCC) is the most anterior cusp, nearest the RVOT and the transducer — cusp 1 in the figure. *(Practice review slide 29.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Using Figure 1, which cusp is the Left coronary cusp?
questions.explanation: The left coronary cusp (LCC) lies posterolaterally, toward the left atrial appendage and pulmonary artery — cusp 2 in the figure. *(Practice review slide 31.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Which of the following is NOT one of the 4 standard views acquired in the PSSAX window?
questions.explanation: The four standard short-axis levels are the aortic valve, mitral valve, papillary muscle, and apex — the pulmonic valve is not one of them. *(Practice review slide 33.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From the parasternal long-axis view, how do you maneuver the transducer to acquire the RVOT?
options: Tilt anteriorly and apply slight clockwise rotation (towards patient’s left shoulder)
Angle toward the patient’s right hip
Angle toward the patient’s left hip
Rotate the probe until the indicator points to the left shoulder
questions.explanation: From PLAX, tilt the transducer superiorly toward the patient’s left shoulder to open the RV outflow tract and pulmonic valve. *(Practice review slide 35.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From the parasternal long-axis view, how do you maneuver the transducer to acquire the RVIT?
options: Rotate the probe until the indicator points to the left shoulder
Tilt toward the patient’s right hip
Angle toward the patient’s left shoulder
Angle toward the patient’s left hip
questions.explanation: From PLAX, tilt inferomedially toward the patient’s right hip to bring up the RV inflow view and the tricuspid valve. *(Practice review slide 37.)*
